title: Bob Woodward on Trump, Nixon and Anonymity

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当 DJ 时，你每天晚上也要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: Bob Woodward's reporting on the Nixon administration pioneered a form of reporting using anonymous sources that has reached unprecedented levels in news coverage of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: Bob Woodward 对尼克松政府的报道开创了一种使用匿名消息源的报道形式，这种形式在如今对特朗普政府的新闻报道中达到了前所未有的程度。

sentences.en: Now, Woodward has deployed that form of reporting to tell the story of this administration in his new book, Fear.
sentences.zh: 现在，Woodward 在他的新书《恐惧》（Fear）中运用了这种报道形式来讲述本届政府的故事。

sentences.en: My colleague Mike Schmidt spoke to Woodward about his process.
sentences.zh: 我的同事 Mike Schmidt 就此采访了 Woodward，了解了他的工作流程。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 9 月 11 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Let's go, because I've got to go home and change and then have to do Colbert tonight.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧，因为我得回家换身衣服，今晚还要去上《Colbert》节目。

sentences.en: I mean, look at the bounce from the most serious man in American journalism, Michael, to the least serious person in American entertainment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看看从美国新闻界最严肃的人 Michael，到美国娱乐界最不严肃的人，这中间的反差有多大。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, you're undermining your own judgment already.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你已经在削弱你自己的判断力了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: How can we do that?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: What we wanted to do was start with you reading the note to readers.
sentences.zh: 我们想从你朗读给读者的那封信开始。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Because we think it gives very important insight into how you did what you did.
sentences.zh: 因为我们认为这能让人非常深刻地洞察你是如何完成这项工作的。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: Ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Okay, this is the note to reader for fear, and it's very short.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是《恐惧》一书的读者寄语，非常简短。

sentences.en: Often these notes are long, and it says,
sentences.zh: 通常这些寄语都很长，它是这样写的：

sentences.en: Interviews for this book were conducted under the journalistic ground rule of deep background.
sentences.zh: 本书的采访是在“深度背景”这一新闻准则下进行的。

sentences.en: This means that all the information could be used, but I would not say who provided it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着所有信息都可以使用，但我不会透露提供者是谁。

sentences.en: The book is drawn from hundreds of hours of interviews with firsthand participants and witnesses to these events.
sentences.zh: 本书取材于数百小时与事件亲历者和见证人的访谈。

sentences.en: Nearly all allowed me to tape record our interviews so the story could be told with more precision.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有受访者都允许我录音，以便更精确地讲述故事。

sentences.en: When I have attributed exact quotations, thoughts, or conclusions to the participants,
sentences.zh: 当我将确切的引语、想法或结论归于受访者时，

sentences.en: That information comes from the person, a colleague with direct knowledge, or from meeting notes, personal diaries, files, and government or personal documents.
sentences.zh: 这些信息来自当事人本人、有直接了解的同事，或是会议记录、个人日记、档案以及政府或个人文件。

sentences.en: President Trump declined to be interviewed for this book.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统拒绝接受本书的采访。

sentences.en: So, in many ways, you're talking about anonymous source reporting and anonymity.
sentences.zh: 所以，在很多方面，你谈论的是匿名消息源报道和匿名性。

sentences.en: And that is an issue that is in the news right now with your book, with the recent op-ed, The Times, ran by an anonymous administration official.
sentences.zh: 这也是目前新闻界关于你的书以及最近《纽约时报》刊登的一篇匿名政府官员评论文章所讨论的问题。

sentences.en: But what people may not realize is that you started this type of reporting at the beginning of your career with Watergate.
sentences.zh: 但人们可能没有意识到，你从职业生涯之初的“水门事件”就开始了这种报道方式。

sentences.en: Why did you first turn towards anonymous sources?
sentences.zh: 你当初为什么转向使用匿名消息源？

sentences.en: You know, first of all, the sources are not anonymous to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，首先，这些消息源对我来说并非匿名。

sentences.en: I know exactly who they are.
sentences.zh: 我非常清楚他们是谁。

sentences.en: So, I think it's, in a sense, the wrong phrase.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为从某种意义上说，这个说法是不准确的。

sentences.en: They are deep background or background sources.
sentences.zh: 他们是“深度背景”或“背景”消息源。

sentences.en: And back, what, 46 years ago, in Watergate, Carl Bernstein and I turned to using unnamed sources because you can't get the truth.
sentences.zh: 回到 46 年前的水门事件，Carl Bernstein 和我开始使用未具名消息源，因为你无法获得真相。

sentences.en: You won't get the straight story from someone.
sentences.zh: 你无法从某人那里得到直接的实情。

sentences.en: If you do it on the record, you will get a press release version of events.
sentences.zh: 如果你公开记录，你只会得到一份新闻稿式的事件版本。

sentences.en: And in Watergate, we wanted, because it was criminal, because it was under the radar, people had to be protected.
sentences.zh: 而在水门事件中，因为涉及犯罪，因为是在暗中进行，人们必须受到保护。

sentences.en: So, this was driven by necessity.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是出于必要。

sentences.en: What necessity, though?
sentences.zh: 是什么样的必要呢？

sentences.en: Necessity to get the real story.
sentences.zh: 获取真实故事的必要。

sentences.en: If you want to position yourself with reality, you can't go up to somebody and say, hey, oh, you're the bookkeeper for all the secret Watergate funds.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解现实情况，你不能直接走到某人面前说，嘿，你是所有水门事件秘密资金的会计吗？

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Where'd they go?
sentences.zh: 钱去哪儿了？

sentences.en: You're going to get a door slammed in your face.
sentences.zh: 你只会吃闭门羹。

sentences.en: When you look back on that reporting, when was the first time that you either realized that you needed it, anonymity, or that you did it?
sentences.zh: 当你回顾那段报道时，你第一次意识到需要匿名性，或者第一次使用它是在什么时候？

sentences.en: When did you dig down and find these folks and start using them?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候深入挖掘找到这些人并开始使用他们的？

sentences.en: Well, interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很有趣。

sentences.en: A couple of days after Watergate, a reporter at the Post, Gene Pashinsky, found out that two of the Watergate burglars had the name of Howard Hunt or H.
sentences.zh: 水门事件发生几天后，《华盛顿邮报》的一位记者 Gene Pashinsky 发现，两名水门事件窃贼的通讯录里有 Howard Hunt 或 H.

sentences.en: Hunt W.
sentences.zh: 亨特·W

sentences.en: House in their address books.
sentences.zh: House 的名字。

sentences.en: It was pretty clear W.
sentences.zh: 很明显 W.

sentences.en: House was the White House.
sentences.zh: House 指的是白宫（White House）。

sentences.en: And I called the White House and got Hunt on the phone and said, why was your name in these address books?
sentences.zh: 我给白宫打了电话，联系上了 Hunt，问他为什么他的名字会出现在这些通讯录里。

sentences.en: And he hung up and left town.
sentences.zh: 他挂断电话并离开了城里。

sentences.en: And there was a kind of, I am packing my bags quality to his voice, which made me suspicious.
sentences.zh: 他的声音里有一种“我正在收拾行李”的感觉，这让我产生了怀疑。

sentences.en: But I can have your name in an address book and go do something nefarious and you may or may not have the connection.
sentences.zh: 但我的名字出现在通讯录里，你可能去做了什么邪恶的事，而我可能与此有关，也可能无关。

sentences.en: So then I called a man named Mark Felt in the FBI, not named, used him as a deep background source, and asked about these address book entries and Howard Hunt.
sentences.zh: 所以我给 FBI 的 Mark Felt 打了电话，没有透露姓名，把他作为深度背景消息源，询问了这些通讯录条目和 Howard Hunt 的情况。

sentences.en: And he said he's in the middle of this.
sentences.zh: 他说他正身处其中。

sentences.en: That's not in the story anywhere, but it's a kind of backstop to the evidence that was in address books.
sentences.zh: 这在报道的任何地方都没有提到，但它是对通讯录中证据的一种支撑。

sentences.en: And Mark Felt turns out to be who?
sentences.zh: 那么 Mark Felt 后来被证实是谁？

sentences.en: Deep Throat.
sentences.zh: “深喉”。

sentences.en: So what you're describing is a unique journalistic moment in which you're reporting on the highest levels of power.
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的是一个独特的新闻时刻，你正在报道最高权力层。

sentences.en: And it was extraordinary in many ways.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这都是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: And this was your best tool.
sentences.zh: 而这是你最好的工具。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's no alternative.
sentences.zh: 而且别无选择。

sentences.en: I mean, suppose there'd been no address book entries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，假设没有那些通讯录条目。

sentences.en: And just Mark Felt saying he was involved was not enough.
sentences.zh: 仅仅靠 Mark Felt 说他参与其中是不够的。

sentences.en: And so you want to get as many sources for any story as you can.
sentences.zh: 所以你希望为任何报道尽可能多地寻找消息源。

sentences.en: And without anonymity, you think Nixon would have survived?
sentences.zh: 如果没有匿名性，你认为尼克松能挺过去吗？

sentences.en: You know, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: We wouldn't have got the most important stories about what Watergate was about.
sentences.zh: 我们可能无法获得关于水门事件本质的最重要报道。

sentences.en: And the whole theme of our reporting in Watergate was it's not about a burglary, one isolated event.
sentences.zh: 我们在水门事件报道中的核心主题是，这不仅仅是一起入室盗窃案，一个孤立的事件。

sentences.en: It's about a massive campaign of sabotage and espionage directed at the Democrats by the Nixon re-election committee in the Nixon White House.
sentences.zh: 这是尼克松竞选连任委员会和尼克松白宫针对民主党进行的一场大规模破坏和间谍活动。

sentences.en: And that opened it up to not just one incident.
sentences.zh: 这让它不再仅仅是一个单一事件。

sentences.en: And it turned out that, of course, Watergate had all these components to it of dirty tricks, fundraising, lying, cover-up, denials that were put forth with great passion.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，水门事件当然包含了所有这些成分：肮脏的勾当、筹款、撒谎、掩盖、以及充满激情的否认。

sentences.en: I remember, and it gets your attention, when the spokesman for the leader of the free world, Ron Ziegler, Nixon's press secretary, called Carl and myself character assassins.
sentences.zh: 我记得，这很引人注目，当自由世界领导人的发言人，尼克松的新闻秘书 Ron Ziegler 称 Carl 和我为“人格刺客”时。

sentences.en: The original fake news?
sentences.zh: 最初的“假新闻”？

sentences.en: Yeah, the original, well, that's, yeah, that's an interesting parallel.
sentences.zh: 是的，最初的，嗯，那是一个有趣的类比。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the same concept that the president employs now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这和总统现在使用的概念是一样的。

sentences.en: It's not that different.
sentences.zh: 没什么不同。

sentences.en: And it's the same strategy of let's make the conduct of the news media the issue rather than the conduct of the president.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是同样的策略：让新闻媒体的行为成为焦点，而不是总统的行为。

sentences.en: How do you think that the outcome of Watergate shaped the public's view of anonymous sources?
sentences.zh: 你认为水门事件的结果是如何塑造公众对匿名消息源的看法的？

sentences.en: That's an important question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的问题。

sentences.en: I think it was an era because eventually Nixon resigned, not because of our reporting,
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一个时代，因为最终尼克松辞职了，不是因为我们的报道，

sentences.en: but because we started a process of the government looking more intensely at what had gone on.
sentences.zh: 而是因为我们开启了一个政府更深入审视所发生之事的进程。

sentences.en: But it ended the sequence in Nixon's resignation.
sentences.zh: 但它以尼克松的辞职结束了这一系列事件。

sentences.en: And so then that gave a stamp of approval to Deep Throat, Mark Felt.
sentences.zh: 所以这给了“深喉”Mark Felt 一种认可。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think that was a good thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: I think you just made an incredibly important point about how your reporting fits into Watergate.
sentences.zh: 我认为你刚才提出了一个极其重要的观点，关于你的报道是如何融入水门事件的。

sentences.en: It's that by writing the stories you did at the beginning, you brought the public's attention to an issue that the government may have ignored otherwise.
sentences.zh: 正是通过撰写你最初的那些报道，你让公众关注到了一个政府原本可能忽视的问题。

sentences.en: Kickstarting a process that leads to the downfall of Nixon.
sentences.zh: 启动了一个导致尼克松下台的进程。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what happened, I remember Sam Irvin, the senator, who set up the Watergate committee before he did it, called me up and said, come see me.
sentences.zh: 当时发生的事，我记得参议员 Sam Irvin，他在成立水门事件委员会之前，把我叫去说，来见我。

sentences.en: And he wanted to know our sources.
sentences.zh: 他想知道我们的消息源。

sentences.en: And I said, I just can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我说，我实在做不到。

sentences.en: And Senator Irvin, to his great credit, said, I understand that, but we're going to launch an investigation anyway,
sentences.zh: 参议员 Irvin 非常大度地说，我理解，但我们无论如何都要展开调查，

sentences.en: because I think there are lots of important unanswered questions here.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这里有很多重要的未解之谜。

sentences.en: And as you know, the Senate Watergate committee was the gold standard of congressional investigations.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，参议院水门事件委员会是国会调查的黄金标准。

sentences.en: They got testimony from everyone.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了所有人的证词。

sentences.en: I mean, it went on for weeks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这持续了数周。

sentences.en: I mean, the network stopped doing soap operas and ran the Senate Watergate hearings back to back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，电视网停止播放肥皂剧，连续转播参议院水门事件听证会。

sentences.en: So I think that there was a sense that you can go from journalism to government action.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当时有一种感觉，你可以从新闻报道走向政府行动。

sentences.en: So do you think that had the outcome of people coming to believe that sometimes anonymity is an absolute necessity for reporting at the highest echelons of power?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这是否导致人们相信，有时匿名对于最高权力层的报道是绝对必要的？

sentences.en: You know, I hope so.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我希望如此。

sentences.en: But look, I understand the skepticism and the regard I have for your work.
sentences.zh: 但听着，我理解这种怀疑，我也尊重你的工作。

sentences.en: When I read one of your stories and you haven't named the sources, I believe you're right, but I don't know you're right.
sentences.zh: 当我读到你的报道而你没有点名消息源时，我相信你是对的，但我并不知道你是对的。

sentences.en: And if you had documents and testimony and FBI reports and photographs and so forth, it would be more powerful.
sentences.zh: 如果你有文件、证词、FBI 报告、照片等等，它会更有说服力。

sentences.en: But you're not going to get that.
sentences.zh: 但你得不到这些。

sentences.en: I can only go with what I got.
sentences.zh: 我只能根据我所拥有的信息来报道。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When you're coming out of the Watergate experience, how do you define this form of anonymity that you created?
sentences.zh: 当你从水门事件的经历中走出来时，你如何定义这种你所创造的匿名形式？

sentences.en: And what were the best ways that it could have been used?
sentences.zh: 以及它能被使用的最好方式是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think the best ways is it gets at the truth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为最好的方式是它能触及真相。

sentences.en: And in doing books on President Clinton, President George W.
sentences.zh: 在撰写关于克林顿总统、乔治·W·布什总统、奥巴马总统的书时，我发现特别是对于布什和奥巴马，我可以工作几个月甚至一年来查明发生了什么。

sentences.en: Bush, President Obama, I found that particularly with Bush and Obama, I could work for months or even a year and find out what happened.
sentences.zh: 从深度背景消息源那里了解发生了什么，然后去找总统说，我想进行这次公开记录的采访。

sentences.en: What happened from deep background sources and then go to the president and say, I want to do this interview on the record.
sentences.zh: 我与乔治·W·布什总统进行了 12 小时的公开记录采访。

sentences.en: And I did 12 hours of interviews with President George W.
sentences.zh: 我能够向他提问。

sentences.en: Bush on the record.
sentences.zh: 关于阿富汗战争的第一本书，对奥巴马也是如此。

sentences.en: I was able to ask him questions.
sentences.zh: 最后，他对我说，你的消息源比我的还好，这当然不是真的。

sentences.en: And the same with Obama on the first book about the Afghan war.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种对该方法的验证。

sentences.en: At the end, he said to me, you have better sources than I do, which, of course, is not true.
sentences.zh: 我从白宫、五角大楼、中情局、国务院和其他地方工作的人那里获得了我询问的信息。

sentences.en: But what that was was a validation of the method.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为他能说出“你的消息源比我的还好”这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: I got the information I got the information I asked him about from people who worked in the White House and the Pentagon and the CIA and the State Department and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果我没有这些深度背景采访，你是做不到这一点的。

sentences.en: And I always thought that was very important for him to say, you have better sources than I do.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: As it was, it was, ah, you couldn't do that if I didn't have these deep background interviews.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是 Andrew Ross Sorkin。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括 J.D. Vance、Elon Musk、Christine Lagarde、Zoran Mondani 等人。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月 18 日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 在我们现在的这个时刻，在媒体中，我们看到匿名消息源的使用可能比以往任何一届政府时期都要多，对吧？

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 你认为这公平吗？

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是事实。

sentences.en: In the moment we're in now, in the media, we've seen anonymous sources used probably more than at any time in a previous administration, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Do you think that's a fair?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为事情变得更加隐蔽了，因为这是触及真相的唯一途径。

sentences.en: I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 在《恐惧》中的信息上周开始传出后，一位在职的关键人物给我打电话说，

sentences.en: Why is that the case?
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你在这里所说的是真的。

sentences.en: Well, because things are more hidden, because it's the only way to get at the truth.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: After the information and fear started breaking last week, one key person who's in office called me and said,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Everyone knows what you've said here is true.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: It's 1,000% correct.
sentences.zh: 这百分之一千是正确的。

sentences.en: And then this person has said some public things that contradict that.
sentences.zh: 而且此人后来发表了一些公开言论，与此相矛盾。

sentences.en: And I'm not happy, but I have a smile on my face because the truth in all of this is going to emerge.
sentences.zh: 我并不高兴，但我脸上带着微笑，因为这一切的真相终将浮出水面。

sentences.en: There's too much evidence, too many witnesses.
sentences.zh: 证据太多了，证人也太多了。

sentences.en: And you know this so well.
sentences.zh: 而且你对此非常清楚。

sentences.en: You have to smoke them out.
sentences.zh: 你必须把他们逼出来。

sentences.en: You have to do stories to get stories.
sentences.zh: 你必须通过报道来获取更多报道。

sentences.en: Was getting inside the room more difficult or easier in this book compared to previous ones?
sentences.zh: 与之前的书相比，这次深入内部获取信息是更难了还是更容易了？

sentences.en: Good question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: I really don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, because some people were quite concerned.
sentences.zh: 我是说，因为有些人非常担心。

sentences.en: I think once you got the ball rolling, getting their participation, it was easier.
sentences.zh: 我想一旦你打开了局面，让他们参与进来，就容易多了。

sentences.en: But I discovered, lo and behold, you have to get into people's homes.
sentences.zh: 但我发现，你瞧，你必须得走进人们的家里。

sentences.en: And I tell this story about calling somebody from the White House at 11 o'clock at night saying, You know, when are we doing that interview?
sentences.zh: 我讲过一个故事，有一次晚上11点我给白宫的人打电话说，你知道，我们什么时候做那个采访？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, we'll talk.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，我们会谈谈的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I said, How about now?
sentences.zh: 我说，现在怎么样？

sentences.en: Now?
sentences.zh: 现在？

sentences.en: It's 11 o'clock at night.
sentences.zh: 现在都晚上11点了。

sentences.en: And I said, Well, I'm four minutes away.
sentences.zh: 我说，我离你那儿只有四分钟路程。

sentences.en: How do you know where I live?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道我住哪儿？

sentences.en: I said, That's the easy part.
sentences.zh: 我说，那是最容易的部分。

sentences.en: Okay, come on over for a while.
sentences.zh: 好吧，过来坐会儿吧。

sentences.en: And it was not dawn, but it was getting close to dawn when I left.
sentences.zh: 我离开时虽然还没到黎明，但也快了。

sentences.en: And I was on the verge at 11 o'clock at night saying to myself, God, screw this.
sentences.zh: 晚上11点的时候，我本来差点就对自己说，天哪，算了吧。

sentences.en: I'm 74 years old.
sentences.zh: 我都74岁了。

sentences.en: I've done this enough.
sentences.zh: 我做这些已经够多了。

sentences.en: Go home.
sentences.zh: 回家吧。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure why, but I instead made the phone call.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么，但我还是打了那个电话。

sentences.en: And if I hadn't made the phone call, my understanding of what has gone on in the Trump White House would be a lot less.
sentences.zh: 如果我没打那个电话，我对特朗普白宫所发生之事的了解会少得多。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about some of the stories that you turned up in your reporting.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈你在报道中挖掘出的一些故事吧。

sentences.en: What's the one that felt the most illuminating to you?
sentences.zh: 哪一个故事让你觉得最有启发性？

sentences.en: I think perhaps a National Security Council meeting December 19th.
sentences.zh: 我想也许是12月19日的国家安全委员会会议。

sentences.en: And I'm going to get the notes of the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我去找一下会议记录。

sentences.en: May I quote from them?
sentences.zh: 我可以引用其中的内容吗？

sentences.en: Is that too?
sentences.zh: 可以吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我看看。

sentences.en: Which one was the?
sentences.zh: 哪一个是？

sentences.en: See, this is the problem when you get so much, so many notes and documents.
sentences.zh: 你看，这就是当你拥有如此多、如此多的笔记和文件时会出现的问题。

sentences.en: At this NSC meeting, the issue is South Korea.
sentences.zh: 在这次国安会会议上，议题是韩国。

sentences.en: And the president says, why are we spending so much money on keeping these troops in South Korea?
sentences.zh: 总统说，我们为什么要花这么多钱在韩国驻军？

sentences.en: We have 28,000 troops, costs about $3.5 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 我们有2.8万名驻军，每年花费约35亿美元。

sentences.en: And he said, I just don't understand that.
sentences.zh: 他说，我就是不明白这一点。

sentences.en: And why are we spending all this money on, say, Taiwan, protecting Taiwan?
sentences.zh: 还有，我们为什么要花这么多钱，比如说，在台湾，保护台湾？

sentences.en: And finally, Secretary of Defense Mattis says, look, we're doing all of this because we're trying to prevent World War III.
sentences.zh: 最后，国防部长马蒂斯说，听着，我们做这一切是因为我们试图防止第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: Now, this, I was really jarred by this, that the Secretary of Defense has to remind the president that part of the job is preventing World War III.
sentences.zh: 现在，这一点让我感到非常震惊，国防部长竟然不得不提醒总统，他的职责之一就是防止第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: And Trump goes on about, you know, we're stupid.
sentences.zh: 特朗普继续喋喋不休地说，你知道，我们太蠢了。

sentences.en: We could be making much more money.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with money on all of this.
sentences.zh: 他沉迷于这一切背后的金钱问题。

sentences.en: And it's misplaced because not only Secretary of Defense Mattis, but they're all saying these
sentences.zh: 这完全是本末倒置，因为不仅是国防部长马蒂斯，他们所有人都说这些

sentences.en: are the best national security dollars we spend, that we should spend 10 times as much money in South Korea if we got these benefits.
sentences.zh: 是我们花得最值的国家安全经费，如果我们能获得这些利益，我们甚至应该在韩国多花十倍的钱。

sentences.en: So that was jarring to me.
sentences.zh: 所以这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: Did you feel that there was more of a motivation amongst the folks you talked to for the book to talk because of fear than in previous books or previous submissions?
sentences.zh: 与之前的书或之前的投稿相比，你觉得这次接受你采访的人是否因为恐惧而更有动力去谈论这些事？

sentences.en: I wouldn't say it was fear.
sentences.zh: 我不会说是因为恐惧。

sentences.en: I would say it was serious concern.
sentences.zh: 我会说是因为严重的担忧。

sentences.en: As I quote Gary Cohen, the chief economic advisor to President Trump in the prologue to the book,
sentences.zh: 正如我在书的序言中引用特朗普总统的首席经济顾问加里·科恩的话，

sentences.en: when he's stealing a draft letter off the president's resolute desk in the Oval Office, he said, got to protect the country.
sentences.zh: 当他从椭圆形办公室总统的坚毅桌上偷走一份草拟的信件时，他说，必须保护这个国家。

sentences.en: He discovers that there's a draft letter to withdraw from the South Korean trade agreement on the president's desk and that the president might sign it and take this action.
sentences.zh: 他发现总统桌上有一份退出韩美贸易协定的草拟信，而且总统可能会签署并采取这一行动。

sentences.en: And so he just took it.
sentences.zh: 于是他就把它拿走了。

sentences.en: And as he told an associate, I did this to protect the country.
sentences.zh: 正如他告诉一位同事的那样，我这样做是为了保护国家。

sentences.en: And Trump won't let go of this issue.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普对这个问题一直不肯放手。

sentences.en: And so finally, Gary Cohen calls in Mattis, the secretary of defense, says you have to talk to the president about this and say we're spending all this money
sentences.zh: 所以最后，加里·科恩叫来了国防部长马蒂斯，说你必须和总统谈谈这件事，说我们花了这么多钱

sentences.en: for our intelligence partnerships and operations and protecting the country.
sentences.zh: 用于我们的情报伙伴关系和行动，以及保护这个国家。

sentences.en: And we can shoot down a North Korean missile in seven seconds because of the capacity that we have.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们拥有的能力，我们可以在七秒钟内击落一枚朝鲜导弹。

sentences.en: And this is at risk.
sentences.zh: 而这一切正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And it is one of those moments.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中一个时刻。

sentences.en: And this is where I conclude that there was a kind of nervous breakdown of the executive power of the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以我得出结论，美国的行政权力出现了一种精神崩溃。

sentences.en: What do you mean by a nervous breakdown?
sentences.zh: 你所说的精神崩溃是什么意思？

sentences.en: A nervous breakdown that you can't have the president who has solely has the executive authority under the Constitution, have staffers deciding, well, no, not this one.
sentences.zh: 精神崩溃是指，你不能让宪法赋予唯一行政权力的总统，由幕僚们来决定，嗯，不，这个不行。

sentences.en: We're going to take some of that away.
sentences.zh: 我们要夺走他的一部分权力。

sentences.en: At the same time, people deemed it sufficiently dangerous to act.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，人们认为这足够危险，必须采取行动。

sentences.en: To me, this seems like one of the most pointed conclusions you have ever made about an administration.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这似乎是你对一届政府做出的最尖锐的结论之一。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: You mean that it's that there is a nervous breakdown?
sentences.zh: 你是说存在精神崩溃吗？

sentences.en: Well, you basically say that the administration is teetering on a catastrophe or a collapse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你基本上是说这届政府正处于灾难或崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: Well, I provide the evidence of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我提供了证据。

sentences.en: And it's just supported by fact, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信这有事实支持。

sentences.en: It's not a partisan position.
sentences.zh: 这不是党派立场。

sentences.en: This isn't about Democrats or Republicans or left, right.
sentences.zh: 这无关民主党人、共和党人，也无关左派或右派。

sentences.en: It's about the stability of the country.
sentences.zh: 这关乎国家的稳定。

sentences.en: And it's not something you can read and feel comforted by.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是你能读完并感到安心的东西。

sentences.en: Do you ever look at the coverage today and think that the anonymous sources are overused?
sentences.zh: 你是否有时会看现在的报道，认为匿名消息来源被过度使用了？

sentences.en: Sometimes, but maybe they're underused.
sentences.zh: 有时是这样，但也许他们被低估了。

sentences.en: And I will tell reporters, I say, you know, anonymous sources, they're not anonymous to you.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉记者，我说，你知道，匿名消息来源，对你来说他们并不是匿名的。

sentences.en: Somebody who really knows something that's important that they can't possibly put their name to in public, but think the public needs to know.
sentences.zh: 那些真正知道重要信息，但无法在公开场合署名，却认为公众有权知道的人。

sentences.en: You know, you call them anonymous sources.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你称他们为匿名消息来源。

sentences.en: I think they're background or deep background sources who are firsthand witnesses are an excellent path to what's really going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是背景或深度背景消息来源，作为第一手证人，他们是了解真相的绝佳途径。

sentences.en: But only part of it, but a vital part.
sentences.zh: 但这只是其中一部分，但却是至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: When you saw the Times op-ed last week by the anonymous administration official, was there anything in there that you would have allowed or used from an anonymous source?
sentences.zh: 当你上周看到《纽约时报》那篇匿名政府官员的评论文章时，里面有什么内容是你作为记者会允许或使用匿名来源的吗？

sentences.en: To be honest with you, because I know this is the New York Times, if that person had come to me and said,
sentences.zh: 老实说，因为我知道这是《纽约时报》，如果那个人来找我说，

sentences.en: this is what I want to say anonymously as a kind of appendix to your book or in your book, I would have said no, because I would have said, what are the specifics?
sentences.zh: 这是我想匿名发表的内容，作为你书的附录或书中的一部分，我会拒绝，因为我会问，具体细节是什么？

sentences.en: What happened when, what was said, what was done, what were the motives?
sentences.zh: 什么时候发生了什么，说了什么，做了什么，动机是什么？

sentences.en: Those are the building blocks of journalism, not a kind of generalized condemnation.
sentences.zh: 这些才是新闻报道的基石，而不是一种笼统的谴责。

sentences.en: Let me ask you the hard question.
sentences.zh: 让我问你一个尖锐的问题。

sentences.en: What would you have done if that person had come to you as a reporter?
sentences.zh: 如果那个人作为记者来找你，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: I think that as a reporter on this story, you would try and build off of it as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为这个故事的记者，你会尽可能地在此基础上进行深挖。

sentences.en: With specifics.
sentences.zh: 用具体的细节。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You say, who's this person?
sentences.zh: 你会问，这个人是谁？

sentences.en: Is it somebody who works in the National Security Council in the White House, somebody in the Pentagon, somebody in the CIA?
sentences.zh: 是白宫国家安全委员会的人，五角大楼的人，还是中央情报局的人？

sentences.en: What do they know?
sentences.zh: 他们知道什么？

sentences.en: And if they were not participants or witnesses to specific decisions and actions and discussions, I don't know what validity they have.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不是具体决策、行动和讨论的参与者或见证人，我不知道他们有什么可信度。

sentences.en: But based on your reporting, can you understand why someone would feel that way and take the extraordinary measure to do something like that?
sentences.zh: 但根据你的报道，你能理解为什么有人会有这种感觉，并采取这种极端的措施去做那样的事吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But these things have to be measured by the quality of the information.
sentences.zh: 但这些事情必须用信息的质量来衡量。

sentences.en: And the quality of the information didn't pass my teSt.
sentences.zh: 而那条信息的质量没有通过我的测试。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know who it is.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不知道那个人是谁。

sentences.en: If it turns out it's somebody who's a key person, that would alter my perspective on it.
sentences.zh: 如果事实证明那是一个关键人物，那会改变我的看法。

sentences.en: But I still would have insisted on specifics.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然会坚持要求提供具体细节。

sentences.en: But again, you know, you've got three people here, right, at the New York Times who know who it is.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，你知道，你在《纽约时报》有三个人，对吧，他们知道那个人是谁。

sentences.en: And maybe it is somebody who has sufficient credentials and experience that they decided to run this.
sentences.zh: 也许那个人确实拥有足够的资历和经验，所以他们决定刊登这篇文章。

sentences.en: And the truth emerges.
sentences.zh: 真相终会大白。

sentences.en: Why does it matter to you how much stature or the position the person has in the administration?
sentences.zh: 为什么那个人在政府中的地位或身份对你来说很重要？

sentences.en: It's not about stature, but it's all about position, because what are they a firsthand witness to?
sentences.zh: 这与地位无关，但与职位有关，因为他们是哪些事件的第一手见证人？

sentences.en: Firsthand source.
sentences.zh: 第一手来源。

sentences.en: But it can be a vicious cycle where these sources are used and then the president attacks it and uses that to undermine it and it gives him ammunition.
sentences.zh: 但这可能形成一个恶性循环，这些来源被使用，然后总统进行攻击并利用这一点来削弱其可信度，这反而给了他弹药。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not sure it undermines it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不确定这会削弱它。

sentences.en: I remember during Watergate, once we joked we had a good story and we said, all we need is a White House denial now to give this credibility.
sentences.zh: 我记得在水门事件期间，我们曾开玩笑说我们有一个好故事，我们说，现在我们只需要白宫的否认来增加可信度。

sentences.en: The president has attacked you on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 总统在推特上攻击了你。

sentences.en: Do you see that as the modern-day validity?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是现代意义上的有效性吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: I mean, look, people have said, oh, how do you feel?
sentences.zh: 我是说，看，人们会说，哦，你感觉如何？

sentences.en: I said, look, he has a right to say what he wants.
sentences.zh: 我说，看，他有权说他想说的话。

sentences.en: He has First Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 他有宪法第一修正案赋予的权利。

sentences.en: And I feel really comfortable with the picture I've presented and the evidence.
sentences.zh: 我对所呈现的图景和证据感到非常坦然。

sentences.en: Hello, Bob.
sentences.zh: 你好，鲍勃。

sentences.en: President Trump, how are you?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统，你好吗？

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: How are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 还好吗？

sentences.en: Oh, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，没关系。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I don't mind.
sentences.zh: 我不介意。

sentences.en: I feel like you had masterfully gotten the conversation you had with him recorded.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你非常巧妙地录下了你和他之间的谈话。

sentences.en: It enabled you to show the lengths you went to to get him to.
sentences.zh: 这让你能够展示你为了让他（接受采访）所付出的努力。

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't particularly masterful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这谈不上特别巧妙。

sentences.en: I just said, I'd like to record this, Mr. President, when he called.
sentences.zh: 他打电话来时，我只是说，总统先生，我想录下这段谈话。

sentences.en: And he said, okay.
sentences.zh: 他说，好的。

sentences.en: So I turned on the tape recorder.
sentences.zh: 所以我打开了录音机。

sentences.en: Who did you ask about speaking to me?
sentences.zh: 你问过谁关于和我谈话的事？

sentences.en: Well, about six people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大约六个人。

sentences.en: Well, they don't tell me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们没告诉我。

sentences.en: But the release of that showed your work.
sentences.zh: 但那段录音的发布展示了你的工作。

sentences.en: It showed what you had done.
sentences.zh: 它展示了你所做的一切。

sentences.en: But are you naming names or do you just say sources?
sentences.zh: 但你是在指名道姓，还是只说消息来源？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it names real incidents.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，它提到了真实的事件。

sentences.en: No, but do you name sources?
sentences.zh: 不，但你提到消息来源的名字了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are you naming the people or just say, you know, people?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你是在点名，还是只说，你知道，人们？

sentences.en: I'd say at 2 o'clock on this day, the following happened.
sentences.zh: 我会说在某天的两点钟，发生了以下事情。

sentences.en: And everyone who's there, including yourself, is quoted.
sentences.zh: 在场的所有人，包括你自己，都被引用了。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry I didn't get to ask you about these.
sentences.zh: 很抱歉我没能就这些问题问你。

sentences.en: I mean, you do know I'm doing a great job for the country.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道我为这个国家做了出色的工作。

sentences.en: And it also showed the president praising you for your previous reporting.
sentences.zh: 而且它还显示总统称赞了你之前的报道。

sentences.en: I've always been fair.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很公正。

sentences.en: You've always been fair to me.
sentences.zh: 你对我一直都很公正。

sentences.en: You know I'm very open to you.
sentences.zh: 你知道我对你非常坦诚。

sentences.en: I think you've always been fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你一直都很公正。

sentences.en: But we'll see what happens.
sentences.zh: 但我们走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: Well, that was last month.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是上个月的事了。

sentences.en: That was last month.
sentences.zh: 那是上个月的事了。

sentences.en: Now he's got a new line this month.
sentences.zh: 现在他这个月有了新的说法。

sentences.en: I believe in our country.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的国家。

sentences.en: And because you're our president, I wish you good luck.
sentences.zh: 而且因为你是我们的总统，我祝你好运。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Bob.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，鲍勃。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Give him credit when I said, I want to record this.
sentences.zh: 当我提出想录音时，得归功于他。

sentences.en: He said, fine.
sentences.zh: 他说，没问题。

sentences.en: And I said to him, we are at a pivot point in history.
sentences.zh: 我对他说，我们正处于历史的转折点。

sentences.en: And his response was right.
sentences.zh: 他的回应是，没错。

sentences.en: But why?
sentences.zh: 但为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is it a pivot point?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一个转折点？

sentences.en: Because Donald Trump is president.
sentences.zh: 因为唐纳德·特朗普是总统。

sentences.en: But being president is about the exercise of power.
sentences.zh: 但担任总统关乎权力的行使。

sentences.en: And when he told Bob Costa and himself, you know, real power, the real stuff is fear.
sentences.zh: 当他告诉鲍勃·科斯塔和他自己时，你知道，真正的权力，真正的东西就是恐惧。

sentences.en: And I've said this, it was almost a Shakespearean aside.
sentences.zh: 我说过，这几乎就像莎士比亚剧中的旁白。

sentences.en: It's almost like Hamlet turning to the audience and saying, this is what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像哈姆雷特转向观众说，这就是一切的意义所在。

sentences.en: What did you understand him to be saying?
sentences.zh: 你认为他想表达什么？

sentences.en: It's all said that you have to scare the daylights out of people to be powerful.
sentences.zh: 这一切都说明，要拥有权力，就必须把人们吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: Today, on the eve of September the 11th, I want to deliver a clear and unambiguous message on behalf of the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天，在9月11日前夕，我谨代表美国总统传达一个明确且毫不含糊的信息。

sentences.en: In his first major speech as National Security Advisor, John Bolton leveled a harsh attack on the International Criminal Court,
sentences.zh: 作为国家安全顾问，约翰·博尔顿在首次重要演讲中对国际刑事法院进行了猛烈抨击，

sentences.en: which has the authority to prosecute genocide and war crimes, saying its very existence violates U.S.
sentences.zh: 该法院有权起诉种族灭绝和战争罪，他称其存在本身就侵犯了美国的

sentences.en: sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 主权。

sentences.en: We will not cooperate with the ICC.
sentences.zh: 我们不会与国际刑事法院合作。

sentences.en: We will provide no assistance to the ICC.
sentences.zh: 我们不会向国际刑事法院提供任何援助。

sentences.en: And we certainly will not join the ICC.
sentences.zh: 而且我们绝不会加入国际刑事法院。

sentences.en: The Trump administration is furious that the International Court, which the U.S.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府对国际法院感到愤怒，该法院由美国

sentences.en: helped create but never formally joined, is considering an investigation into U.S.
sentences.zh: 协助创建但从未正式加入，目前正在考虑对美国的

sentences.en: military action in Afghanistan that could result in the prosecution of American soldiers.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗军事行动进行调查，这可能导致美国士兵被起诉。

sentences.en: We will let the ICC die on its own.
sentences.zh: 我们将任由国际刑事法院自生自灭。

sentences.en: After all, for all intents and purposes, the ICC is already dead to us.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，从所有意图和目的来看，国际刑事法院对我们来说已经名存实亡了。

sentences.en: In a statement, one of the court's founders, David Sheffer, said that Bolton's speech, quote,
sentences.zh: 在一份声明中，该法院的创始人之一大卫·谢弗表示，博尔顿的演讲，引用他的话，

sentences.en: isolates the United States from international criminal justice and severely undermines our leadership in bringing perpetrators of atrocity crimes to justice elsewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 将美国与国际刑事司法隔离开来，并严重削弱了我们在世界其他地方将暴行罪犯绳之以法方面的领导地位。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争之中。
